turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Who decided to give him a zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for agreeing to meet in person.
Thanks are fine, Hale, but I'm still waiting on my answer. Who decided on the zero, and was it before or after anyone spoke to Owen? I'm writing down what you say.
I'll admit I looked you up. Your firm's appellate record is remarkable.
Don't manage me, Hale. You looked me up before you called me about my son's zero, but you still haven't answered who decided it.
Someone with your training will appreciate that I'm simply following the evidence. I expect you'd do the same in my position.
I'd do it in the right order, Hale: speak to the student, call the parent, then enter a mark. What evidence? Name it, with dates, and I'll write it down.
